story_description: As a developer building hooks, I need per-provider event type definitions so that the hook system validates events correctly for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI, and I can write type-safe hook handlers that know which events and matchers are available for each provider.
task_description: Define HookProvider enum, HookEventType per-provider enums, HookMatcher patterns, and HookCapability structs in HookSchema.swift that encode the complete event vocabulary for each supported CLI provider including blocking capabilities and matcher patterns.
atom_description: Create comprehensive Swift type definitions in HookSchema.swift encoding all hook event types for Claude Code (12 events), Gemini CLI (11 events), and Codex CLI (2 notify events), including which events support blocking, which matchers are valid per event, and tool name mappings between providers.
problem_statement: The hook system currently has no type-safe representation of which hook events exist for each CLI provider. Without per-provider event definitions, the hook builder cannot validate event names, cannot filter matchers appropriately, cannot indicate which events support blocking responses, and cannot support cross-provider hook migration with correct event name mapping.
scope_in: HookProvider enum with cases claude, gemini, codex representing supported CLI providers

ClaudeHookEventType enum with 12 events: SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, Notification, PermissionRequest, ErrorOccurred, ContextCompacted
GeminiHookEventType enum with 11 events: BeforeTool, AfterTool, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, BeforeModel, AfterModel, BeforeToolSelection, SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreCompress, Notification
CodexHookEventType enum with 2 events: AgentTurnComplete, ApprovalRequested
HookEventCapability struct defining canBlock, availableMatchers, description per event
HookToolNameMapping struct for cross-provider tool name translation
Static dictionaries mapping event types to their capabilities per provider
scope_out: Hook execution logic - handled by HookRunner in separate atom
Hook configuration persistence - handled by MultiProviderHooksService
Hook builder UI - handled by HooksBuilderView atoms
Hook migration utilities - handled by H007-MIGRATE atom
Runtime event dispatching - handled by engine adapters
assumptions: Swift enum with associated values provides sufficient type safety for event modeling
Each provider has a fixed set of events that does not change at runtime
Codex CLI notify events are not true hooks but can be modeled similarly for UI consistency
Tool name mappings are static and known at compile time from CLI documentation
constraints: Must use Swift enums for type safety and exhaustive switch handling
Must be Codable for persistence and IPC
Must be Sendable for actor isolation in hook service
Must support CaseIterable for UI enumeration
Event names must match exactly what CLIs expect in configuration files
functional_requirements: FR-01: HookProvider enum distinguishes between claude, gemini, and codex CLI backends
FR-02: Each provider has dedicated event type enum with all supported events
FR-03: HookEventCapability struct indicates if event can block execution flow
FR-04: HookEventCapability includes array of valid matcher patterns per event
FR-05: HookEventCapability includes human-readable description for UI display
FR-06: HookToolNameMapping provides bidirectional mapping between provider tool names
FR-07: Static factory methods return capabilities for any event on any provider
FR-08: Events that take matchers define valid matcher patterns as enum or string array
FR-09: SessionStart events include startup, resume, clear, compact matcher options
FR-10: Tool events include tool name patterns as matchers
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-01: All types must be Sendable for safe concurrent access
NFR-02: All types must be Codable for JSON serialization
NFR-03: Enum raw values must match CLI config file expectations exactly
NFR-04: Type definitions compile to zero runtime overhead via static dispatch
NFR-05: Documentation comments on each type for code completion hints
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create HookProvider enum with cases claude, gemini, codex and rawValue String matching CLI names
Step 2: Add HookProvider computed properties for displayName, configFileName, and supportsBlocking
Step 3: Create ClaudeHookEventType enum with all 12 Claude Code events as cases with String raw values
Step 4: Add ClaudeHookEventType computed property canBlock returning true for UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest
Step 5: Add ClaudeHookEventType computed property matcherType returning SessionStartMatcher, ToolMatcher, or nil
Step 6: Create GeminiHookEventType enum with all 11 Gemini CLI events as cases with String raw values
Step 7: Add GeminiHookEventType computed property canBlock returning true for BeforeTool, BeforeAgent, BeforeModel, BeforeToolSelection
Step 8: Add GeminiHookEventType computed property matcherType for tool and session matchers
Step 9: Create CodexHookEventType enum with 2 notify events: agentTurnComplete, approvalRequested
Step 10: Add CodexHookEventType computed property canBlock always returning false
Step 11: Create HookEventCapability struct with canBlock, matchers, description, and provider fields
Step 12: Create SessionStartMatcher enum with cases startup, resume, clear, compact for session lifecycle events
Step 13: Create ToolMatcher struct with pattern String for glob-style tool name matching
Step 14: Create HookToolNameMapping struct with from, to provider fields and tool name dictionaries
Step 15: Add static HookToolNameMapping.claudeToGemini and HookToolNameMapping.geminiToClaude instances
Step 16: Create HookEventRegistry struct with static methods to get all events for a provider
Step 17: Add HookEventRegistry.capabilities(for event, provider) returning HookEventCapability
Step 18: Add Codable, Hashable, Sendable conformances to all public types
Step 19: Add documentation comments with event descriptions and matcher examples
Step 20: Write unit tests verifying event counts, blocking flags, and matcher associations

edge_cases: Unknown event type string from config file: return nil from init?(rawValue:) and handle gracefully
Provider does not support blocking: canBlock always returns false for all events
Tool matcher pattern is empty: treat as match-all pattern
Codex provider selected: show only 2 notify events, indicate no blocking support
Event name case sensitivity: rawValue must match CLI expectations exactly
failure_modes: JSON decoding fails for unknown event: Codable init throws, wrap in try/catch
Event enum exhaustive switch incomplete: compiler error catches at build time
Tool name mapping missing entry: return nil and use original name as fallback
Memory allocation for static registries: negligible, all types are value types
rollback_plan: Delete HookSchema.swift, HookToolNameMapping.swift, and HookEventRegistry.swift. Remove HookProvider enum if only used by this atom. Hook builder falls back to hardcoded event strings without type safety. Existing hook configurations remain valid JSON but lose compile-time validation.

risks: CLI providers may add new events in future versions requiring schema updates
Event names in documentation may have typos causing runtime mismatches
Tool name mappings may be incomplete for less common tools
Breaking changes to CLI hook format require coordinated schema updates
mitigations: Pin to specific CLI versions in compatibility matrix and test against them
Validate event names against actual CLI config parsing in integration tests
Document known tool mappings and provide fallback to original name for unknown tools
Add version field to HookProvider for future format migration support
risk_register.blast_radius: Low impact - affects only hook configuration validation. Invalid events fail gracefully at config load time. Core session functionality unaffected.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If schema types cause issues, replace with simple String-based event names and Dictionary-based capabilities. Lose compile-time safety but maintain runtime functionality.

persistence: No direct persistence; types are Codable for JSON serialization in hook config files
Hook configurations using these types persisted via MultiProviderHooksService
